$comment: The SessionEnd capture hook, declared in the PLUGIN MANIFEST (referenced from .claude-plugin/plugin.json). When Backthread is installed as a Claude Code plugin, this registers the hook automatically AT USER/GLOBAL SCOPE — no mutation of the user's project .claude/settings.json, and it fires across EVERY repo AND git worktree (a per-project, gitignored .claude/settings.json hook is exactly what silently stops capturing — worktree sessions never carry it; an installed plugin's hooks follow the user, not the cwd). The command invokes the plugin's BUNDLED, self-contained bin via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (dist-bundle/backthread.js — committed to git so the marketplace-cloned plugin has it; CC runs no build step on install), NOT `npx backthread`, which would resolve a possibly-stale or absent global / npm-linked install (the other half of the same silent-stall failure). The detached worker re-spawns via process.execPath + process.argv[1], so pointing argv[1] at the bundle propagates the same self-contained bin through the WHOLE chain (hook → detached worker). It routes through the shared `--from-hook` entrypoint with `--detach`: it reads the SessionEnd payload off stdin, then re-spawns a DETACHED worker that does the slow LOCALLY-redacted redact→infer→persist round-trip and returns immediately — so a ≥30s inference can't be SIGTERM'd by CC's SessionEnd hook timeout (or reaped on session exit). Best-effort, never blocks/delays the session, always exits 0. `--agent claude-code` selects the CC payload shape. Mirrored by the USER-SCOPE ~/.claude/settings.json fallback that `backthread install` writes for the bare-npx (non-plugin) path. We register BOTH SessionEnd (a once-per-session backstop) AND Stop (per-turn) — see $comment_stop.
$comment_stop: The per-turn CAPTURE hook: `Stop` fires at every assistant turn-end, so a decision is captured as the work happens — held (merge-gated) until its branch merges, then RELEASED by the merge webhook, so merged decisions surface in Backthread mid-session instead of waiting for SessionEnd. Same bundled command as SessionEnd (the shared `--from-hook` entrypoint + `--detach`); `runCapture` already handles a Stop payload and `hook_event_name` is purely informational. This was previously left UNregistered as 'too aggressive', but the per-conversation incremental WATERMARK (keyed on session_id) makes each fire infer ONLY the turns added since the last capture (O(N) over a session, not O(N²) or a re-capture-everything) — the exact mechanism Cursor & Codex already run per-turn in production. SessionEnd stays as a backstop: the watermark dedups, so the final SessionEnd fire is a no-op when the last turn's Stop already captured everything, and it still catches a session killed without a final Stop.
$comment_sessionstart: The SessionStart AMBIENT-ROUTING hook. Injects a one-time instruction into the session context telling Claude Code to call the `query` MCP tool FIRST on how/why-does-X questions, before grepping — so a plain 'how does X work?' routes to a grounded, cited answer with no new user habit. SYNCHRONOUS, NOT --detach: CC reads this command's STDOUT for hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, so the bundle must print it (a detached re-spawn would print an ack instead). It does only a FAST LOCAL config read (no network), gates on a present device token (only routes when `query` can actually answer), and always exits 0 with valid JSON. PLUGIN-ONLY: runs the shipped self-contained bundle (fast, offline); the bare-npx settings.json fallback deliberately does NOT register it, because a synchronous `npx backthread session-start` would block every session start on npm's resolve (the capture hook only gets away with @latest because it's --detach'ed). npx-fallback users keep the `query` tool's imperative description.
$comment_pretooluse: The PreToolUse GREP-CONTEXT hook — the local tier of the two-tier grep-time context hook. When CC is about to run Grep or Glob, this reads the search term off the payload and injects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext = a ~300-token join of the repo-local STRUCTURE cache (`backthread graph`) + the merged decision WHY cache (`backthread sync`) for that term — so the agent sees the relevant modules AND the recorded why at the moment it goes looking, with NO per-grep network/LLM/billing. The why riding alongside the structure is the point (structure alone would just be parity with a structure-graph tool). matcher `Grep|Glob`. SYNCHRONOUS (CC reads this STDOUT) so it runs the shipped self-contained BUNDLE, NOT --detach; it does ONLY a fast local cache read + a pure join (no extractor, no network), so it can't meaningfully delay the grep. FAIL-OPEN: an empty `{}` (no cache / no match / any hiccup) = no injection, grep proceeds; it never blocks (never exits 2, never emits a permissionDecision) and always exits 0. PLUGIN-ONLY for the same reason as SessionStart: a synchronous `npx backthread grep-context` would block EVERY grep on npm's resolve, so it is never written to the ~/.claude/settings.json fallback.
$comment_pretooluse_edit: The PreToolUse PRE-EDIT hook — the one line offered before someone changes an area they have no coverage of. matcher `Edit|MultiEdit|Write`. It asks the Worker's /coverage-preflight ONE question (repo slug + one repo-relative path; no source, the file is never opened) and, at most ONCE PER SESSION and ONLY on a clean 200 `signal:'uncovered'`, returns a single `systemMessage` line pointing at /backthread:how. Everything else — `covered`, `unresolved`, any non-200, a network error, a timeout, a malformed body, no device token, a non-git cwd — is SILENT, the same fail-toward-silence posture as captureScope.ts's `interpretScopeResponse` with the polarity flipped: a line shown because a lookup hiccuped is a false accusation about someone's own codebase. It NEVER blocks the edit — short timeout, no permissionDecision, never exits 2, always exits 0 — because interrupting a coding flow is the fastest way to get uninstalled. A session also gets a small LOOKUP budget (not just one line), so a session on a well-covered repo does not pay for a round-trip on every single edit. SYNCHRONOUS + PLUGIN-ONLY for the same reasons as the grep hook: CC reads this STDOUT, and a synchronous `npx backthread` would block every edit on npm's resolve, so it is never written into the ~/.claude/settings.json fallback.
$comment_posttooluse_inflow: The PostToolUse DEAD-TIME hook — one optional question about this codebase, delivered at the one moment the person has nothing to do: their agent has just finished a Bash / Task / WebFetch / WebSearch step and they are waiting on the next one. matcher `Bash|Task|WebFetch|WebSearch`. It asks the Worker's /inflow/ask ONE question (repo slug + the trigger name; no source, no file, no path) and, at most ONCE PER SESSION and only on a clean 200 that actually carries a question, injects hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext telling the agent to relay it at its next natural break — and to drop it silently and permanently if it is ignored. IT IS A PostToolUse HOOK AND MUST STAY ONE, AND ITS MATCHER MUST NEVER NAME AN EDITING TOOL: firing before a tool, or around Edit/MultiEdit/Write, would put a question between somebody and the file they are about to change, which is exactly the toll gate this trigger was forbidden to be. The command also re-checks the tool name against its own closed allowlist, so the property holds even if this matcher is edited. Everything else — no question in the reply (by far the common case), any non-200, a network error, a timeout, a malformed body, no device token, a non-git cwd — is SILENT, the same fail-toward-silence posture as the other courtesy hooks. NOTHING IS PERSISTED ABOUT THE ASK on either side: /inflow/ask performs no writes at all, the question exists only inside the short-lived signed token in the reply, and this hook writes only an opaque session id to its own once-per-session ring — identical bytes whether a question came back, none did, or the request failed, so 'asked and ignored' and 'never asked' are indistinguishable locally too. SYNCHRONOUS + PLUGIN-ONLY for the same reasons as the grep and edit hooks: CC reads this STDOUT, and a synchronous `npx backthread` would block on npm's resolve. Short timeout, always exits 0.
